title: Formulation and Characterization of Primary Tissue-Derived Microfluidic Droplet-Engineered Organoids
author: Wanlong Wang
materials: Formulation and Bioprinting of Cell-Laden Microspheres (Figure 3)
Lamination of Organoids for Rapid Characterization (Figure 4)
Turn on the sterilization switch of the equipment and activate the UV sterilization for 20 min.
Culture organoid precursors/cellular spheroids in a 96-well plate.
Install the microscope slide on the lamination device.

steps.title: Sterilize workspace and equipment
steps.instruction: Work inside a sterile laminar‑flow biosafety cabinet; UV‑irradiate the cabinet and all equipment for 20 min before starting. Keep the cabinet temperature between 20–25 °C during the procedure.

steps.title: Prepare tissue fragments on ice
steps.instruction: Using sterilized forceps and scalpels, cut the primary tissue (e.g., mouse liver) on ice into small fragments of approximately <1 mm size. Place the fragments into a 60 mm diameter Petri dish containing 2 mL DPBS with 2 % penicillin/streptomycin (P/S).

steps.title: Wash tissue with DPBS
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue fragments three times with DPBS containing 2 % P/S, gently inverting the dish each time.

steps.title: Grind tissue using sTED device
steps.instruction: Open the grinding chamber of the automated small‑Tissue Extraction Device (sTED) and add the tissue fragments with forceps. Run the device through its six automated steps:

substeps.instruction: a) Select grinding mode and lower the upper grinding plate until the grinding surfaces fuse.
b) Add grinding buffer, set the lower plate to rotate at 60 r/min and run for 1 min.
c) Lift the upper plate 10 mm to separate the plates.
d) Add 10× tissue digestion reagent, rotate the lower plate at 60 r/min for 5 min at 37 °C.
e) Pass the resulting cell suspension through a 100 µm cell filter.
f) Add an equal volume of digestion‑termination reagent (contains 10 % serum) to stop the reaction.

steps.title: Terminate digestion and lyse red blood cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension (speed not specified), discard the supernatant, then add 2 mL red blood cell (RBC) lysis solution to the pellet, pipette gently and incubate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend primary cells
steps.instruction: Re‑centrifuge the suspension, remove the supernatant, and add 2 mL culture medium to the cell pellet. Pipette up‑and‑down to obtain a homogeneous primary cell suspension. Then resuspend the cells in 1 mL basal culture medium and keep on ice for 1 min.

steps.title: Count cells with AO/PI staining
steps.instruction: Prepare an AO/PI working premix containing 50 µg/mL propidium iodide (PI) and 10 µg/mL acridine orange (AO) in DPBS. Aspirate 10 µL of the cell suspension and 10 µL of the AO/PI premix, mix, and load onto a hemocytometer for counting.

steps.title: Prepare cell‑Matrigel bioink
steps.instruction: Keep Matrigel on ice. Using a pre‑cooled 100 µL pipette tip, aspirate the required volume of Matrigel, dispense into an Eppendorf tube, and gently mix with the cell suspension (1 mL basal medium) by pipetting up‑and‑down. Maintain the mixture at 4 °C, avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles, and use within 2–4 h if not printed immediately.

steps.title: Sterilize and set up OrgFab printer
steps.instruction: Place the OrgFab printer inside the biosafety cabinet. Turn on UV sterilization for 20 min. Ensure the software temperature setpoint is 4 °C before starting. Verify that the ventilation of the cabinet is active (20–25 °C ambient).

steps.title: Install microfluidic chip and tubing
steps.instruction: Install the microfluidic chip onto the semiconductor cooling platform. Connect the two oil inlet ports, one bioink inlet port, and one droplet outlet port with PTFE tubing. Install the print head, connecting one end to the collection/incubation tubing and the other end to the high‑pressure gas line. Place the EP tube containing the bioink in the sample tank and insert the bioink tubing. Install the collection tubing in the heating chamber, linking the droplet outlet port to the print head.

steps.title: Load bioink and oil flows for droplet generation
steps.instruction: Run the following automated sequence (steps a–h) on the OrgFab printer:

substeps.instruction: a) Lower the mechanical turntable to fix the chip on the cooling platform.
b) Pump oil into both oil inlet channels at 312.5 µL/min to fill and purge air from the chip.
c) Aspirate bioink from the EP tube and infuse the bioink channel at 250 µL/min while simultaneously pumping oil out of the front‑right inlet.
d) Rotate the turntable knob to switch the bioink channel to the front‑left outlet.
e) Pump oil again: 312.5 µL/min through Oil inlet 2 and 25 µL/min through Oil inlet 1.
f) Shear the bioink flow with the co‑flowing oil to generate uniform cell‑laden droplets (microfluidic droplet encapsulation).
g) Stop oil pumping, store the droplets in the collection tubing, and solidify the Matrigel droplets at 37 °C for 30 min.

h) Pump oil at 12.5 µL/min (Oil inlet 1) and 25 µL/min (Oil inlet 2); the camera‑based visual detection triggers high‑pressure gas bursts that eject one solidified droplet into each well of a 96‑well plate. Each well receives the desired number of droplets.

steps.title: Culture printed organoid precursors
steps.instruction: Place the 96‑well plate with printed organoid precursors into a 37 °C CO₂ incubator. Change the culture medium every other day for 7–14 days until organoids are fully grown.

steps.title: Prepare drug stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each test drug to a 50 mM stock solution, filter through a membrane, and aliquot 5 µL per sterile tube. Store stocks protected from light.

steps.title: Perform serial drug dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the highest‑concentration drug stock in culture medium to create a 5‑fold serial dilution series. Calculate the exact volumes of drug stock and medium required for each step.

steps.title: Add drug‑containing medium to organoids
steps.instruction: Replace the existing medium in each well with the appropriate drug‑containing medium (ascending concentrations). Use three replicate wells per concentration and reserve one well per concentration for live/dead staining. Perform medium changes every other day to prevent drug degradation.

steps.title: Measure viability with CTG assay
steps.instruction: After 5 days of drug exposure, add 100 µL CellTiter‑Glo (CTG) reagent to each well, place the plate on a shaker for 2 min, and record luminescence with a microplate reader. Incubate the plate at room temperature for 10 min before reading. Construct an IC₅₀ curve from the luminescence data.

steps.title: Perform live/dead staining
steps.instruction: After 6 days of drug exposure, prepare a Calcein‑AM/PI working solution by mixing 900 µL ddH₂O, 100 µL 10× assay buffer, 1 µL 2 mM Calcein‑AM, and 3 µL 1.5 mM PI. Aspirate all medium from the designated live/dead wells, wash with DPBS, add the staining solution, and incubate at room temperature in the dark for 5 min. Wash again with DPBS and image under a fluorescence microscope.

steps.title: Laminate organoids onto spatial chip
steps.instruction: For each organoid to be profiled:

substeps.instruction: 1) Pick the organoid with a Pasteur pipette under a microscope.
2) Wash the organoid three times with 1× SSC buffer.
3) Add cell‑recovery solution, incubate at 4 °C for 15 min.
4) Wash with 1× SSC, add cell‑dissociation reagent, incubate at room temperature for 2 min.
5) Load the organoid onto the spatial‑transcriptomics chip using a Pasteur pipette.
6) Use a gas cylinder to gently blow and dry liquid around the organoid (avoid complete desiccation; retain a thin water film).
7) Cover the chip with a 3 cm × 3 cm PTFE film using tweezers (avoid wrinkles).
8) Install the chip on the lamination device, place a glass slide on top, and add a weight.
9) Rotate the device knob to lift the chip until it contacts the glass slide.
10) Remove the weight and glass slide vertically, then heat the chip at 37 °C for 5 min.
11) Use tweezers to lift and discard the PTFE film without disturbing the laminated cell layer.

steps.title: Optional immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: After lamination, perform standard immunofluorescence staining (e.g., DAPI) on the 2‑D organoid layer and image at 100 µm scale bar.
